author: rodneykinney
quote: I'm interested to know how often the solution involves a non-optimal HTR, where there are things like slice insertions that only affect same-color edges. Ordered route classes: S1 normal, linear 2qt, HTR length = shortest linear 2qt on normal (+ extensions up to +1?); S2 normal, linear 2qt 4b2->4a1->HTR any length; S3 normal, linear 4qt HTR of length <=8; S4 normal: reductions to 4a1 of minimal length and +1,+2, then |sw| (NISS) -> HTR (route 4b2->4a1 |sw| ->HTR, switch after 1st qt); S5 normal: shortest regressions 4b2->2c3 2e/4e (written, then |sw| ->4b2->4a1->HTR, 4qt switch after first qt); S6 = S1-S5 on inverse; S7 = NISS HTRs from S4/S5/S6; S8 2+2 NISS: 4b2->2c3 or 4b2->4a1 then |sw| ->new 4b2->4a1->HTR, or 4b2->4a1->0c0 (not 0e) |sw| ... author: Lewis Isom
quote: Starting with 4a2 2e/0e (if you have 4a2 with 4e, then it's a lot easier). List of things to check: 1) Linear 2qt HTRs on both sides. This means the first qt makes 4a1 4e. 2) Write down all the +1's and +2's to 4a1 4e, and NISS them. 3) Try U/U' M2 U and U/U' S2 U on both sides to see if there's an easy linear 4a2 4e case afterwards. 4) Now onto 4qt stuff with 4c3. Basically the idea with this one is you go: 4a2 -> 4b3 NISS 4a3 >Parity Fix> 4b2 -> 4a1 -> HTR First write down all the ways to regress to 4c3 with 2e/4e in +1 or +2 moves on both sides. Don't go to 4c3 0e because it can't be +7 to HTR after NISS. Next NISS all of those and try solving HTR. Best you can hope for is +3 to slice post-HTR. Alternatively, you could NISS trace the pieces/do bounding instead of actually NISSing, but you'd have to memorize 7/8 move 4c3 HTR shapes which is kind of not worth it. 5) The final thing you can try is to regress to 0c3. For this, only try +1's to 0c3 and try both linear HTR and NISS HTR from there. Should be pointed out that this gives +11 to HTR linearly and +10 w/ NISS, so it is pretty dire at this point. Additionally, 0c3 2e and 6e can be +9 after NISS, but 0e, 4e, and 8e are +10. 6) Stop looking at this DR and move on to checking your other DRs now.
what_to_compute: 4a2 2e and 4a2 0e. S1: linear 2qt 4a2 -> 4a1 4e -> HTR, normal or inverse; S2: reductions 4a2 -> 4a1 4e in minimal length +1/+2 (length = min reduction +1, +2), then |sw| -> HTR; S3: U M2 U / U S2 U style (qt, slice, qt: 4a2 -> 4b? -> 4a2 4e, 2 extra qt) then linear 4a2 4e -> 4a1 -> HTR (4qt linear), both sides; S4: regress 4a2 -> 4b3 (2e/4e, not 0e) in +1/+2 moves, |sw| (now 4a3), U2-parity fix, 4a3 -> 4b2 -> 4a1 -> HTR (4qt, switch after 1st qt); S5: regress 4a2 -> 0c3 in +1, then linear or NISS HTR (0c3 -> 4a2 -> 4a1 -> HTR, 4qt); S6 stop. Grade cumulative share of 4a2 0e/2e states whose optimal is found by S1..Sk. Side claims to check separately (next rows).

author: Lewis Isom

Additionally, 0c3 2e and 6e can be +9 after NISS, but 0e, 4e, and 8e are +10.
what_to_compute: From 4a2 2e/0e: (a) for 4c3 0e states reached by a +1/+2 regression, min NISS HTR length (after switch) >7; (b) on route 4a2 -> 4b3 |sw| 4a3 -> 4b2 -> 4a1 -> HTR, min post-HTR leave-slice length >=3; (c) 4a2 regressed in +1 to 0c3: min HTR length counted from the 4a2 state = 11 linear, 10 NISS; (d) for 0c3 xe: min NISS HTR length 9 for 2e/6e, 10 for 0e/4e/8e (unclear whether counted from 0c3 or from 4a2 including the +1).

author: Jay (vibing)
quote: I had a 10 move DR with 3qt corners but the HTR was 2C0E which is annoying. … there's actually not too many things you need to check if you want to try every possible two half turns followed by a quarter turn. You essentially abuse the fact that U2 R2 F and D2 L2 B are HTR equivalent when generating things to NISS for … Things I would have had to check to cover all 0-2 moves to 4C4E 2QT then switch F L2 F U2 F D2 F R2 F L2 U2 F L2 D2 F L2 R2 F U2 L2 F U2 R2 F U2 D2 F If I did this correctly then this means you would have to check 11 total things. You could also skip the last 3 to save time since they're guaranteed to be +3 moves [T330] Anyways, in this specific case it's possible to arrive at optimal for the DR using D2 F and then switch, provided you modify the D2 F later on
what_to_compute: 2c3 0e (old 3qt 2C0E; DR on F/B, DR ended in L). Route class: 0-2 half turns + one DR-axis qt reaching 2qt 4c4e (= 4b2 4e, since 2c3 0e can only reduce to 4b2 4e, D9369), then |sw| and solve 4b2 4e -> 4a1 -> HTR on the other side. Jay's 11 prefixes = {F, L2 F, U2 F, D2 F, R2 F, L2 U2 F, L2 D2 F, L2 R2 F, U2 L2 F, U2 R2 F, U2 D2 F} in his DR orientation. Grade: share of 2c3 0e states where some optimal finish has this form (switch after first qt, prefix 0-2 ht); compare with prefixes restricted to rodney's sets (next row).

Also F R2 U2 R2 F and F R2 D2 R2 [T340] It’s only a single swap or a double swap [T343] Totally agree that it’s only worth going from 3qt to 4qt if you can do it without a setup move [T344] But I do find the inverse prediction useful because you get four NISS's for the price of one.
what_to_compute: Same route class as Jay's (2c3 0e -> one qt to 4b2 4e -> |sw| -> 4a1 -> HTR), prefix sets: rodney-9 = {F, M2 F, S2 F, R2 F} + corner-swap insertions into R2 F (D2 L2 F, D2 R2 F, U2 L2 F, U2 R2 F, L2 ... ); rodney-4 if corner-swap-equivalent prefixes are merged; rodney-2 = {F, R2 F} with inverse prediction covering F R2 L2 B', F R2 U2 R2 F, F R2 D2 R2 premoves. Claims: U2 F-type prefixes are the wrong hyper-parity case (never reach the right 4b2); the 2/4/9 sets cover all NISS-distinct cases of Jay's 11 (same set of reachable 4b2 4e inverse states up to edges). author: beef beans
quote: Bounding update: after lots and lots of solves this is how I use it 0c0: Yes 4a1: if you get a 4a1 case randomly, bound it. Otherwise it's not great. For the 2e/6e case it's not great because you 99% of the time you want to find a 0c0 or 4b2 trigger 4a2: yes yes yes amazing muah chief's kiss 4b2: just check the really short ones, and then just try triggers for the rest 2c3: I only use it for the 6e subset now. Triggers will get you optimal usually for 2e and 4e. Although if I get like 8 to 2c3 or 9 to 2c3 then I'll still bound it because I want to 100% get optimal 4c3: Bounding is actually REALLY good for 4c3. On the b corners side there are sooooo many finecky ways to reduce to 4a1 in very few moves, and bounding can find optimal off of all of them really quickly. Don't do it on the A side of the scramble becuase you need 3 half turns before your next qt after reducing to 4b2 [T7078, Yura] and 2c3 6e if you really have to do it
what_to_compute: Bounding route class B = reduce to 4a1 4e (prefix on normal and/or inverse, any length <=k), switch, finish 4a1 4e -> HTR on the other side. Per subset (0c0, 4a1, 4a2, 4b2, 2c3 by edges, 4c3 split a side vs b side): share of states with some optimal finish of class B (k<=4, <=5), vs share with an optimal via short triggers (linear 2qt/3qt trigger route with <=2 setup moves). Claims: B good for 0c0, 4a1 (but 2e/6e prefer 0c0/4b2 trigger ~99%), 4a2 (best), 4c3 from the b side (4b3 -> 4a2 -> 4a1 4e |sw|), 2c3 6e; triggers suffice for 2c3 2e/4e and most 4b2; on the 4c3 a side, after 4a3 -> 4b2 one needs 3 half turns before the next qt.

author: rodneykinney
quote: Today, I realized that 4a3 corners is, philosophically speaking, a 5qt case in which two of the U moves are adjacent. By which I mean: Setup: U2 F2 U R2 U R2 U2 F2 U Solution: U R2 U // 2c3 corners Now, 2c3 corners has 3 distinct corner solutions (that differ by more than just a slice/corner-swap). … The third one is, of course, just the 3qt solution. The 4a3 case is painful in general because there are so many possibilities for that R2 U2 F2 step in the 3qt solution. I now think it might be easier to just always go to 2c3 and solve from there.
what_to_compute: 4a3 side of 4c3 (all edges). Route classes: R3 = 3qt 4a3 -> 4b2 -> 4a1 -> HTR (with the R2 U2 F2 parity step), R5 = 5qt 4a3 -> 4b2 -> 2c3 -> 4b2 -> 4a1 -> HTR (U R2 U to 2c3, then any 2c3 corner skeleton). Compute share of 4a3 states with some optimal in R3, in R5, and in R5 restricted to linear; and share where every 3qt optimal equals an R5 skeleton with two adjacent U moves merged. Claim: going through 2c3 is easier (findability), not a share.

[T11209, bpaul] certainly not 2c3 8e [T11210, bpaul] if you're including the qt in the 2 moves then there's a 2c3 2e case that cant reduce to 4b2 2e in 2 moves setup U' R2 U R2 U' F2 B2 [T11212, Zagros] i think this is the only 2c3 6e case where you can't [T11213] that's the saving grace for 2c3 6e, always lots of ways to get 4b2 2e

author: Fanti / mrauo / Yura Riabov
quote: [D9369, Fanti] do you have 2c3 0e or 8e? if so then you can only reduce to 4b2 4e [D9440, mrauo] How often 3qt DR's require going through 4b4e instead of 4b2e for optimal finish?? [D9442, Yura] From experience: every time you don't check that

author: Yurii Riabov (Hitchhiker's Guide to HTR)
quote: 2c3 2e is basically the best case you can get except 4a1 4e and some of 0c0 cases, because if 2 bad corners are on different layers it’s always 5-7 moves to triple dr(in some cases depending on parity it is more than 7 to HTR, but still a cool stat)
what_to_compute: 2c3 2e states with the two bad corners on different U/D layers: shortest linear sequence to triple DR (corners in HTR or fake HTR, edges oriented on all axes) is 5-7 for every state; share where shortest HTR > 7.

author: Yurii Riabov (Hitchhiker's Guide to HTR)
quote: As a general rule, if there is a reduction or regression in 1-2 moves to 0c0, 4a1, 4a2 4e, 4b2 or 2c3 2e/4e you should try doing this reduction and spamming corresponding triggers, as well as switching the reductions. … [4a1] after regression to 4b2 2e in 1-2 moves / after reduction to 0c0 2e or 0c0 4e in 1-2 moves(though you should niss trace edges and decide whether to switch based on that) / after regression to 4b2 4e in 1 move … [4b2 2e] after regression to 2c3 2e or 4e in 1-2 moves / after reduction to 4a1 in 1-3 moves if niss trace is good … [2c3] after reduction to 4b2 2e in 1-2 / after reduction to 4b2 4e in 1 … [2c3 6e] after reduction to 4b2 2e in 1-3 / after reduction to 4b2 4e in 1-2 / after reduction to 4a1 4e in 3-4 if niss trace is good
what_to_compute: Switch lists = route classes 'one qt step reached with k moves then |sw|': 4a1: ->4b2 2e (k<=2), ->0c0 2e/4e (k<=2), ->4b2 4e (k=1); 4b2 2e: ->2c3 2e/4e (k<=2), ->4a1 (k<=3); 2c3: ->4b2 2e (k<=2), ->4b2 4e (k=1); 2c3 6e: ->4b2 2e (k<=3), ->4b2 4e (k<=2), ->4a1 4e two qts (k<=4). Grade per subset: share of states whose optimal is linear-with-triggers or one of these switch classes.

author: Yurii Riabov (Hitchhiker's Guide to HTR)
quote: [4a2] after reduction to 4a1 4e in 1-4, for 3-4 only if niss trace is good … [4b3/4a3] after reduction to 4b2 2e in 1-3 / after reduction to 4b2 4e in 1-2 / after reduction to 4a2 4e in 1-2 / after reduction to 4a1 4e in 3-4, niss tracing is also a good idea here … [2c4] after reduction to 2c3 2e or 4e in 1-2 / after reduction to 4b2 2e in 3-4, but only after checking all 2c3 2e and 4e reductions with niss / after reduction to 2c3 6e if you’re desperate … [4b4/4a4] after reduction to 4b2 2e in 3-4, from both sides of the scramble / after first qt of progress in 1-2 … [2c5/4b5] after reduction to 2c4 in 1-2 / after reduction to 2c3 2e or 4e in 3-4
what_to_compute: Switch classes: 4a2: ->4a1 4e (k<=4); 4c3: ->4b2 2e (k<=3), ->4b2 4e (k<=2), ->4a2 4e (k<=2), ->4a1 4e (k 3-4); 2c4: ->2c3 2e/4e (k<=2), ->4b2 2e (k 3-4), ->2c3 6e; 4c4: ->4b2 2e (k 3-4) both sides, first qt of progress (k<=2); 2c5/4b5: ->2c4 (k<=2), ->2c3 2e/4e (k 3-4). Grade share of states whose optimal lies in the union (plus linear).

author: Rodney Kinney
quote: 4QT 3-1: "This case can be solved in 2QT, but the optimal solution often uses 4QT, so we treat it as a separate case." … 5QT: "These are almost never worth bothering with. I would only consider cases where a U* turn leads directly to the 2-0 HTR-4QT case." … I think a good cutoff is 8 moves for the corner skeleton plus insertions, which leaves a couple of moves for the setup to the skeleton and the HTR finish.
what_to_compute: (a) 2qt subsets whose bad corners split 3-1 across U/D (4b2 3-1 shape): share where optimal uses 4qt; (b) 5qt subsets: share of optimal finishes whose first qt leads to 2c4 with bad corners 2-0 (stacked on one face); (c) share of states whose optimal finish has a corner skeleton plus insertions (HTR part minus setup) <=8 moves.

author: Jayden McNeill (ottozing)
quote: 1qt 4CXE often needs 3qt unless it's specifically 4C4E (even then, you should consider 3qt here). … for 2bqt you'll often need to NISS to find short solutions. … with 3qt 2CXE you can always reach 2qt by simply turning it into 4CXE regardless of how many half turns you insert before doing so … but with 4qt 2CXE you need to be careful not to accidentally "reduce" to 5qt 2CXE. … 2bqt - … If it's 4C4E then solutions like U R2 U2 F2 U are possible. Otherwise … optimal solutions often show either tricky 4qt non NISS solutions, or complex 2qt NISS solutions.
what_to_compute: 4a1 0e/2e: share where every optimal uses >=3qt; 4a1 4e: share with a 3qt optimal. 4a2 (old 2bqt) 0e/2e: route shares of optimal: 4qt linear vs 2qt NISS (switch after 1st qt) vs 2qt linear.

author: Aneurin / Adri / Jayden McNeill
quote: [D375, Aneurin] A 1qt corners with 4c2e is going to need 3qt [D3050, Adri] Also 1qt is useless if it's not 4e4c right ? [doc 494] On DR's that only need 1-2 quarter turns to reach HTR, it's not uncommon to have little success by sticking to 1-2 quarter turn solutions. Expanding your search to 3-4 quarter turn solutions might be the key to finding optimal or close to optimal for a given DR
what_to_compute: 4a1 2e: share of states where every optimal uses >=3qt (structurally all, since 1qt needs 4e). 0-2qt subsets: share with an optimal using +2qt (3-4qt).

author: trangium
quote: yeah for 4q and up, no extra qts is likely optimal, but for anything below that is pretty likely to have 2 or even 4 extra qts
what_to_compute: Per subset: share of states with an optimal finish using the minimum qt (no extra qt). Claim high for 4-5qt subsets, low (likely +2/+4) for 0-3qt subsets. Said in DR-fe context; test on plain DR.

author: rodneykinney
quote: It's really quite rare to get to HTR from 3/4qt in less than +2
what_to_compute: 3qt and 4qt subsets: per state, shortest HTR length minus the optimal corner-skeleton length of its corner case (penalty); share with penalty <=1 (claim rare).

author: trangium
quote: [T11189] actually, from normal dr we have a nearly as strong correlation: sample size = 1000 avg opt from DR - qt break (samples) 3f: 12.00 (1) 4f: 12.17 (6) 5f: 12.64 (11) 6f: 13.00 (55) 7f: 13.22 (129) 8f: 13.70 (183) 9f: 14.31 (249) 10f: 14.75 (240) 11f: 15.15 (103) 12f: 15.14 (22) 13f: 16.00 (1) [T11192] note: sample sizes for each cell are quite small (20 to 100) [T11194] also, qt break not included for this one

author: trangium / FakeMMAP / Daichi
quote: [T11428, trangium] you can get a true 2q bound by taking (shortest htr on one side) + (moves to set up to 1qt on the other) [T11431] for the bound to be valid, you need the *fewest* possible moves to set up to 1q on the other side (which might not come from the shortest htr) [T11457, Daichi] Idk how well this bounds 4b2 0e, because HTR is always 6-9 moves and setup is always 0-3 moves, so the bound you’re gonna get is 6-12 moves, when 90+% of 4b2 0e cases are 12-14 optimal
what_to_compute: 4b2 0e: distribution of shortest HTR (claim always 6-9) and min setup to 1qt on the other side (0-3); share with OPT in 12-14 (claim 90+%). Validity of the 2q bound: for 2qt finishes, length >= shortest HTR on one side + fewest moves to reach 4a1 4e on the other.
